tasks.title: Render the emergent ecology: wire scent field + scent-steering + a predator/prey scenario so creatures visibly hunt/herd
tasks.prompt:
Make the already-built emergent-ecology AI substrate drive VISIBLE creature movement in a runnable scenario. The deterministic substrate exists and is unit-tested (see test/ai/ecology_demo_test.cpp for the exact composition that works): ScentField (deposit/diffuse/evaporate/clamp/GradientSteer), RunScentDepositOnTick, RunScentSteeringOnTick, RunInstinctLocomotionOnTick (boids+flee+seek), PerceptionSystem, and the components SensableComponent/PerceptionComponent/AwarenessComponent/ScentSenseComponent/LocomotionProfile/LocomotionIntentComponent in components/InstinctComponents.h. The movement->render path (already exists): main_server.cpp ~L1920 calls RunInstinctLocomotionOnTick -> set_avatar_wish_velocity -> PhysicsSystem::update_avatars (Jolt CharacterVirtual) -> ServerWorldRunner mirrors position into TransformComponent -> GBufferPass renders.

DO:
1) GameSession OWNS a ScentField (std::unique_ptr, GATED: created only when ecology is enabled via a setter/config so the canonical headless roster is byte-identical -> world_hash unchanged when disabled). Add a getter. In GameSession::TickSimulation, when the field exists, run a new slot AFTER the perception slot (2b): RunScentDepositOnTick -> field.Step(0.25, 4, 0.004) [rate is CAPPED at 0.25 — do not exceed] -> field.Clamp(tau_min, tau_max). Pick a world->grid origin (spawn anchor) + cell_size; expose them.
2) In main_server.cpp, right AFTER RunInstinctLocomotionOnTick and BEFORE set_avatar_wish_velocity, call RunScentSteeringOnTick(registry, gameSession.GetScentField(), origin_x, origin_z, cell_size) when the field is enabled, so the scent gradient biases the wish that physics consumes.
3) Add a predator/prey demo scenario to RuntimeScenarioHarness (a new scenario name, e.g. 'ecology_hunt') that enables the ecology scent field and spawns: a few PREY creatures (grovestrider mesh; SensableComponent{scent_channel=0, scent_deposit>0, faction=2}; LocomotionProfile; a wander/flee setup) and a PREDATOR (grovestrider mesh; ScentSenseComponent{channel=0, sign=+1, weber_k~2}; PerceptionComponent{faction=1}; LocomotionProfile move_speed faster). Spawn them with Transform+SkinnedMesh+AnimationPlayer like the existing creature spawn (~RuntimeScenarioHarness.cpp:6487) so they RENDER, plus the AI components so they MOVE under the server tick.

CONSTRAINTS: deterministic (id-ordered, float-only, DeterministicMath::Sqrt, no libm transcendentals/no wall-clock on the tick); the scent field gating MUST keep the canonical headless world_hash byte-identical when ecology is OFF (verify the NetworkStateHash / world-hash gate tests still pass unchanged). NEVER push.

VERIFY (required before claiming done): prepend C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin to PATH; `cmake --build build -j 3` clean; `ctest --test-dir build -j3 -E ShieldRtFarField` must be 100% (the world-hash/determinism gates included — prove ecology-OFF is byte-identical). Report the build + ctest output.

tasks.title: Fix the FarLodHorizon #45 sliver: discard/clamp the grazing far-LOD frustum-edge streak without introducing horizon gaps
tasks.prompt:
Fix issue #45 (FarLodHorizon sliver). The frontier gate currently FAILS: a thin (~1px wide, ~151px tall) FAR-ATTRIBUTABLE terrain streak rasterizes above the eye-level horizon at the frustum edge (a far-LOD triangle viewed near-grazing). The existing radial clip (FarLodSystem kFarClipOuterRadiusMeters=950) does NOT remove it. The far-LOD meshes render via the g_buffer geometry shader; the far path is identified in g_buffer.frag by `u_farClipInnerRadius > 0.0`.

The gate metric is kFarLodHorizonMaxFarAttributableSliverPx=64 (scales to ~142px at native via CaptureScale); current ~151px FAILS. Root cause: far triangles near the camera far-plane / frustum-edge corner rasterize as a tall thin sliver crossing into the sky.

DO: implement a far-LOD-fragment discard for the sliver class WITHOUT introducing visible horizon GAPS (do not blanket-discard legitimate far mountains above the horizon). Candidate approaches (pick what passes the gate): (a) a tighter fragment-level far-distance cap in the u_farClipInnerRadius>0 path; (b) discard far fragments whose geometric normal is near-perpendicular to the view ray (grazing edge-on slivers) AND that project above the estimated horizon; (c) clamp far-vert projection. Tune against the gate. A wrong fix that creates horizon gaps is WORSE than the sliver — verify no new WorldVisualSweep defects.

CONSTRAINTS: render-only (do NOT change world_hash); deterministic. NEVER push.

VERIFY (required before claiming done — do NOT claim fixed otherwise): prepend C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin to PATH; build `cmake --build build -j 3`; then run the actual gate `pwsh? no -> powershell` — run `.forge/scripts/validate-engine-frontier.ps1 -Mode FarLodHorizon` and it MUST exit 0 (currently it throws 'farlod horizon (mountains) analysis reported failure'). Also run `-Mode WorldVisualSweep` to confirm no new visual defects, and `-Mode PlayerView` for no horizon gaps. Paste the FarLodHorizon analysis JSON (max_sky_sliver_px) before/after.
